hero.title: Business Analyst Resume Skills: *90+ skills* for your resume
hero.lede: The business analysis skills hiring managers and ATS actually scan for in 2026 — requirements engineering, process modeling, data analysis, and the stakeholder communication that connects business to delivery. Organized by category and experience level, with real examples of how to phrase them. Explore the list, or generate a set tailored to you.

quickAnswer.question: What skills should a business analyst put on a resume?
quickAnswer.answer: Lead with the core craft — requirements gathering, requirements analysis, and documentation — then process modeling (BPMN, workflow analysis) and data analysis (SQL, Excel, a BI tool). Show the methodologies you work in (Agile, Waterfall), the tools you use (Jira, Visio), and the stakeholder communication that ties business needs to delivery. Tailor the exact mix to the industry and seniority you're targeting.

categories.title: Requirements Engineering
categories.lead: The heart of the BA role — and the most-scanned skill area. Name the artifacts you produce.

categories.title: Process Analysis & Modeling
categories.lead: How you map and improve the way work gets done. A strong differentiator for BAs.

categories.title: Data Analysis
categories.lead: Increasingly central to the role. List the query and reporting skills you actually use.

categories.title: Documentation & Modeling
categories.lead: How you make requirements unambiguous. Diagrams and specs that engineers can build from.

categories.title: Methodologies
categories.lead: The delivery frameworks you work within. Most BA roles are Agile, hybrid, or both.

categories.title: Tools

categories.title: Certifications

mistakes.title: Vague “requirements” with no artifacts.
mistakes.detail: Name what you produce — BRDs, user stories, use cases, acceptance criteria.

mistakes.title: No data skills.
mistakes.detail: Modern BA roles expect SQL and Excel at minimum. Leaving them off dates your resume.

mistakes.title: Listing duties instead of skills.
mistakes.detail: “Attended meetings” is a task. The skill is elicitation, facilitation, stakeholder management.

mistakes.title: No business impact.
mistakes.detail: Tie your work to outcomes — cost saved, errors reduced, process time cut.

mistakes.title: Only technical, no business (or vice versa).
mistakes.detail: A BA bridges both. Show you understand the business case and the delivery detail.

mistakes.title: Ignoring methodology.
mistakes.detail: Agile vs Waterfall matters to teams — state how you work, since it's often a filter.

skillsToAvoid.heading: Skills you usually don't need to list
skillsToAvoid.description: For modern business analyst roles these are assumed or too generic — including them dilutes your stronger skills. Leave them off unless a specific posting explicitly asks.

faq.q: How many skills should a business analyst put on a resume?
faq.a: Aim for 12–16 skills across requirements, process modeling, data analysis, and methodology, plus tools and any certification. Enough to show you bridge business and delivery, but curated to what you can defend with a real project.

faq.q: What are the most important business analyst skills?
faq.a: Requirements gathering and analysis are the core, followed by business process modeling, data analysis (SQL and Excel), and documentation (user stories, use cases, UML). Stakeholder management and clear communication tie them together, and Agile fluency is expected in most roles.

Increasingly, yes. Many BA roles now expect you to pull and analyze your own data rather than wait on an analyst, so SQL and Excel appear in most job descriptions. If you know SQL, list it with a hint of depth (“SQL — joins, aggregations”); it's a strong differentiator.

faq.q: Should I list BABOK or a BA certification?
faq.a: Yes, if you hold one — ECBA, CCBA, CBAP, and PMI-PBA are keywords recruiters filter on, and BABOK knowledge signals you know the discipline's framework. Put certifications near the top and include ones you're actively pursuing if the role values them.

faq.q: What skills should a junior business analyst include?
faq.a: Focus on fundamentals you can demonstrate: requirements gathering, user stories, process mapping, Excel, documentation, and a tool like Jira. Back them with a project you supported. At entry level, evidence you can capture and organize requirements clearly beats claiming senior-level strategy work.

faq.q: How is a business analyst resume different from a data analyst one?
faq.a: A business analyst centers on requirements, process modeling, and bridging stakeholders to delivery, with data analysis as support. A data analyst centers on SQL, statistics, and BI tools to produce insight. If you're transitioning toward data, emphasize the SQL and reporting work; toward BA, emphasize requirements and process.

faq.q: How do I tailor business analyst skills to a job description?
faq.a: Read the posting and note whether it leans requirements, process improvement, or data, plus the methodology and tools it names. Mirror those in your own true words and move them toward the top of your skills section, since ATS ranks you partly on how well your resume echoes the job's language.
